learning_outcomes.text: Explain the specific techniques for the analysis, modeling and simulation of electrical systems.

Efficiently use information sources and communication resources and assisted professional training (Internet portals, specialized software applications, databases, online courses, etc.) both in Romanian and in a language of international circulation.

Familiarize students in the field of Electrical Engineering with knowledge in theoretical electrical engineering and present electromagnetic phenomena in terms of applications in high frequency technology.
Present calculation methods, in a unitary framework, which are necessary to solve problems in classical or modern electrical engineering.
Familiarize students with practical aspects regarding the operation of high frequency electrical systems through the design part.

syllabus_topics: General principles on microwave devices and equipment
Behavior of dielectric materials in the microwave field and theoretical considerations regarding the microwave heating mode
Presentation of the phenomenon corresponding to losses in dielectric materials
Drying and heating of dielectrics in the microwave field.
Microwave generators and their propagation mode
Modeling of electromagnetic and thermal phenomena in the resonant cavity and the sample body
Design of output circuits and protection and safety circuits. Magnetic circuit design
Realization of the assembly scheme for a microwave drying installation
teaching_methods: Free exposure with presentation (online or live, video projector)

assessment_methods.method: Course Exam (Questionnaire on-line or live with 9 subjects)
Project (Free presentation with interactive discussion, online)

assessment_rules: The final exam note (Nfe) is calculated as 0.8 times the course exam note (Nse) plus 0.2 times the project note (Np), i.e., Nfe = 0.8*Nse + 0.2*Np. A minimum mark of 5 is required for the course exam. A minimum mark of 6 is required for the project (Np >= 6). For the project, achieving a grade of 6 implies going through the design stages; for a grade of 10, all design stages must be completed, including calculations and wiring diagrams.
